newsitem.title: UK: Copper lurches lower by end of thin LME session.
newsitem.headline: Copper lurches lower by end of thin LME session.

text.p: Copper jerked lower in thin holiday trade on Friday afternoon after failing to hold firmer levels and most of the other metals moved in tandem.
Three month copper prices took a quick look at a high of $2,165 per tonne in the morning, but were unable to sustain the upside momentum and drifted lower.
A breach of $2,150 after lunch triggered some sell-stops and prices lurched lower, ending the afternoon kerb with a loss of $17 at $2,127.
The premium of cash over three months metal also softened from $105 in the morning to $95/$100 by the afternoon close.
Support is pegged at $2,120/25, then at $2,077/80.

No LME stocks data were released on Friday due to the holidays. The next inventory report scheduled for Tuesday, when traders will be concentrating on copper levels in Singapore after the last report showed a delivery of 4,100 tonnes.

Aluminium also rose in the morning, peaking at $1,570 resistance before falling back to end the day at $1,546, down $11. Analysts said aluminium needed to break back above the up trend line, which was at $1,563 on Friday.
Support is seen at $1,540, then at $1,506/7.
Nickel edged down to a fresh 2-1/4 year low of $6,476 and ended there, suffering a $4 loss.
Analysts say the damaged technical picture makes more weakness likely, with targets of $6,340 and $6,200 expected.
Tin shed $50 to $5,730, descending back towards a 19-month low of $5,680 hit on December 16.
Lead lost $6 to $713 but zinc bucked the trend and finished $3 higher at $1,075 after peaking at $1,080, the highest since November 27.
